# Results — Study 534 (Revenue-Surprise-Drift)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — Jegadeesh &
Livnat (2006): **post-earnings drift follows the revenue (sales) surprise, not just the EPS
surprise, and adds information beyond it** — rebuilt as a clean event study on a fixed
large-cap basket. For each quarterly revenue figure (EDGAR, frame-tagged calendar quarters) we
form the **standardized unexpected revenue** (SUR = seasonal random-walk surprise / its own
trailing volatility), sort events into SUR quintiles, and measure the forward 1 / 5 / 20 / 60-day
drift of the top-minus-bottom long-short — entering the close **one day after the 10-Q/10-K
filing is public** (no look-ahead). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes (30 long-listed US large-caps) + **EDGAR** `companyconcept` quarterly revenue (`data.sec.gov`, public, no key) |
| Window | filings **2013-02-11 → 2026-06-03** (**13.3** years; price tape 4,901 days) |
| Events | **592** quarterly revenue events across **29** names (one name dropped on thin frame-tagged coverage) |
| Surprise | **SUR** — standardized unexpected revenue: `(Rev_q − Rev_{q−4}) / std(prior seasonal diffs)`; ≥8 prior seasonal differences required |
| Drift / entry / costs | enter the close **1 day after** the first session on/after the filing date (no look-ahead); hold 1/5/20/60 days; **10 bps** one-way × 4 legs + **50 bps/yr** borrow on the short leg |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The basket is 30 names *still trading* in 2026.
> A fixed surviving-names panel cannot include firms that were delisted or blew up after a bad
> quarter, which tilts the *long* (sales-beat) leg mildly up and softens the *short* (miss) leg.
> Jegadeesh-Livnat use the full Compustat/IBES cross-section; our large-cap survivor basket is a
> deliberately conservative, transparent slice, and we say so. **Data limitation:** EDGAR
> frame-tagged revenue only goes back to ~2009–2013 for most names and coverage is uneven across
> firms that re-tagged the revenue concept — so this is a *thinner* sample (592 events) than the
> EPS-PEAD study 363 (2,576), and the drift estimates are correspondingly noisier.

## The signal — drift of the SUR long-short (top quintile − bottom quintile)

1-day entry lag; the long-short pools the top-quintile drifts (long) against the bottom-quintile
drifts (short). The *t* is a one-sample *t* of the per-event long-short sample against 0; the
placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 **SUR-label shuffles** whose random top-minus-bottom drift
**beats** the observed one.

| horizon | n events | top mean | bottom mean | long-short | win-rate | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | 592 | +0.15% | +0.02% | **+0.13%** | 51% | +0.59 | 0.281 |
| 5-day  | 592 | +0.47% | +0.82% | **−0.35%** | 51% | −0.70 | 0.751 |
| 20-day | 586 | +1.50% | +1.04% | **+0.46%** | 50% | +0.49 | 0.320 |
| 60-day | 542 | +2.81% | +3.96% | **−1.15%** | 53% | −0.75 | 0.732 |

Read it plainly: **no horizon clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** — the largest *t* anywhere is
**+0.59** (1 day), and the 5- and 60-day spreads are actually **negative**. The cross-section is
not monotone either (20-day drift low → high SUR quintile:
**+1.04% · +2.80% · +1.73% · +0.50% · +1.50%** — the *second* bucket is the highest, the top
bucket is mid-pack). On this large-cap survivor basket, sorting on the **revenue** surprise does
**not** produce a drift you can stand behind.

## Costs — academic only, and it doesn't survive them either

Every event is a fresh round trip on both legs. We charge **10 bps one-way × 4 legs** plus
**50 bps/yr** borrow on the short leg over the holding period.

| horizon | gross long-short | net of costs |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1-day  | +0.13% | **−0.27%** |
| 5-day  | −0.35% | **−0.76%** |
| 20-day | +0.46% | **+0.02%** |
| 60-day | −1.15% | **−1.67%** |

Net of costs the only non-negative number is a **+0.02%** crumb at 20 days — round-trip costs
on four legs erase the already-insignificant gross spread. There is nothing to deploy.

## Robustness — it doesn't survive the bucket count either

| quintile count | long-short (20-day) | *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 3 (terciles) | −0.44% | −0.59 | 0.717 |
| **5 (quintiles)** | **+0.46%** | **+0.49** | **0.320** |
| 10 (deciles) | −0.01% | −0.02 | 0.501 |

The sign of the 20-day spread **flips with the bucket count** (negative for terciles, ~zero for
deciles) — the hallmark of noise, not signal. A **within-quarter block placebo** that shuffles
SUR labels *inside each calendar quarter* (respecting filing-season clustering) gives
**p = 0.582** at 20 days — squarely in the middle of the null. Nothing here is distinguishable
from a random sort.

## Third axis — does revenue surprise add information *beyond* EPS? (Jegadeesh-Livnat's claim)

Jegadeesh-Livnat's central contribution is that the **revenue** surprise drifts *independently
of the EPS surprise*. We test it directly: match each revenue event to the same name's reported
EPS surprise (from study [363](../363-pead-drift)'s cache, ±25 days), then run the SUR
long-short **within EPS-sign strata** — if revenue carried incremental information, the SUR sort
should still pay even after the EPS surprise's sign is held fixed.

| EPS stratum | n events | SUR long-short (20-day) | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| within EPS **beats** | 488 | −0.30% | −0.35 |
| within EPS **misses** | 72 | −0.67% | −0.19 |
| **pooled** | 560 matched | **−0.19%** | **−0.40** |

Both strata are **negative and insignificant**; pooled, the within-EPS SUR long-short is
**−0.19% at *t* = −0.40**. On this basket there is **no** incremental revenue drift once the EPS
surprise's sign is controlled — the Jegadeesh-Livnat incremental claim does **not** replicate
here (a result fully consistent with McLean-Pontiff post-publication decay and with the
conservative, liquid, survivor universe).

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

On a deterministic panel with quarterly filings whose post-event path carries a *known* planted
drift, the long-short inference behaves exactly as it must:

| planted edge | events | long-short (20-day) | one-sample *t* | placebo *p* | win-rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 1,224 | +0.02% | +0.03 | 0.494 | 48% |
| **+0.08** (large planted drift) | 1,224 | +5.38% | **+9.55** | **0.000** | 67% |

With **no** planted drift the test sits at *t* ≈ 0 (it does **not** manufacture significance from
noise); a large planted drift lights up at *t* = 9.55. The control proves the measurement is
unbiased and well-powered — so the flat real-tape result (max *t* = 0.59) is a genuine **absence
of signal on this basket**, not a broken detector. The engine would have found a real drift had
one been there.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Sorted on the standardized unexpected revenue, the top-minus-bottom drift
  **never clears *t* = 2** at any horizon (max **t = +0.59** at 1 day; the 5- and 60-day spreads
  are **negative**), the cross-section is non-monotone, the sign flips with the bucket count, and
  a within-quarter block placebo sits at **p = 0.582**. The faithful synthetic control (zero edge
  → *t* = 0.03, planted edge → *t* = 9.55) shows the detector works — there is simply no revenue
  drift to find on this 30-name survivor basket. Literature support (Jegadeesh-Livnat 2006) is
  **not** enough on its own. NONE, not WEAK.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of one-way costs × per-event turnover (+ borrow), every horizon
  is essentially zero-or-negative (best is **+0.02%** at 20 days). There is no gross edge to erode
  and nothing to deploy. MIRAGE.
- **"Adds info beyond EPS"? — BUSTED.** Within EPS-sign strata the SUR long-short is **−0.19% at
  *t* = −0.40** (negative in both the beat and miss subsets). The specific Jegadeesh-Livnat
  incremental-information claim does **not** replicate on this conservative large-cap survivor
  basket — the revenue surprise carries no drift here that the EPS surprise didn't already.
